title: All-hands: model retirement + migration bridge plan (scratch)
content:
Goal: draft quick, conversational talking points + Q&A for Friday’s all-hands about retiring legacy hosted model variants (redwood-1.0 family) and the bridge plan for customers and internal teams. This is a scratchpad — keep super informal.

Top-level TL;DR (one-liner for exec):
- We are retiring the oldest hosted model variants (redwood-1.0 and friends) to reduce maintenance overhead, improve latency/cost consistency, and simplify the catalog. We will provide a migration bridge (compat variants + compatibility router) and customer support for a 90-day transition window.

Why this matters (for the company):
- Operational complexity: multiple kernel combos, long-tail bugs, and patch churn on 1.0 paths.
- Economics: older weights and execution paths cost ~25% more per token at current throughput due to less efficient kernels and lack of new quantization profiles.
- Product consistency: rolling forward to a smaller set of actively-maintained variants makes SLAs, benchmarking, and perf guarantees realistic.

What we will say at all-hands (high-level talking bullets):
- Thank you for shipping and supporting those models — they powered a lot of early success.
- As models and runtime optimizations matured, a small number of old variants became a drag on reliability and cost.
- We will retire the legacy variants on 2025-01-15 (target); customers will see a deprecation notice starting 2024-11-15.
- Migration path: an automated compatibility router, a recommended mapping table, and a compatibility-testing harness in the console.
- No user data will be deleted; only the hosted variant names are removed. Customers can pin model checkpoints for Private/Dedicated.

Proposed timeline (ops-friendly):
- 2024-11-15: Begin customer and docs comms (email + console banner).
- 2024-12-15: Opt-in compatibility router (traffic mirrored to new variants, no charge).
- 2025-01-15: Retirement of hosted redwood-1.0 variants; traffic auto-route to recommended variants unless customer objects.
- 2025-04-15: Final enforcement and console cleanup for accounts that haven’t migrated.

Customer impact tiering (how we will prioritize support):
- Tier A (enterprise with Dedicated/Private + SLA): Account team outreach + 1:1 migration planning.
- Tier B (high-usage hosted customers): Proactive email + console migration tool + SRE playbook.
- Tier C (low-usage/free tier): Console banner + self-serve docs + community forum posts.

SRE/infra actions (short checklist for on-call/ops):
- Feature flag: create fast rollback for router mapping (JIRA-ENG-4721).
- Canary run: mirror 5% traffic from redwood-1.0 -> redwood-latency-v2 for 48 hours before 12/15 opt-in.
- Metrics to watch: request errors (5xx), p50/p95 latency delta, token cost per req, KV cache miss rate.
- Runbook: if error rate > 2x baseline, pause router and open dedicated incident channel (#inc-legacy-models).

Talking points for product/CEO (script style, short):
- CEO: "We’re simplifying our model catalog so we can focus on delivering predictable performance and lowering costs for our customers. For teams that rely on older variants, we’ve built a bridge to make migration painless."
- Product lead: "We audited usage and cost — <20% of traffic uses the legacy family, but they account for outsized operational burden. Our plan minimizes interruption while letting us invest in features customers ask for."

Anticipated tough questions + suggested answers (prep bullets):
- Q: "Will outputs change?" 
  A: Most customers will see negligible changes. We tested on customer prompt sets and have per-customer similarity reports available in the console. If outputs differ meaningfully, we’ll open a rollback or provide a tuned pinned variant.
- Q: "Can we keep the old variant?"
  A: For Dedicated/Private you can pin existing checkpoints. Hosted variants will be retired for maintainability; we provide compatibility router as an interim for hosted customers.
- Q: "What about cost increases?"
  A: New recommended variants are overall cheaper per token; some customers with specific prompt profiles may see different cost — we’ll surface cost delta per account in the migration tool.
- Q: "How will this affect latency SLAs?"
  A: Our expectation is improved consistency; latency targets will remain the same and we will monitor deviation during the mirroring phase.

Internal asks (who does what before Friday):
- Comms: one-paragraph email + console banner copy (Meera) — due 2024-10-07.
- Docs: migration guide + mapping table + quick-check script (Rafael) — draft by 2024-10-10.
- SRE: add metric dashboard + incident channel (Jun) — 2024-10-09.
- Sales/CS: playbook + pre-built migration checklist for Tier A (customer-facing) (assigned: Sarah L.) — 2024-10-11.

Open questions / things to lock down this week (notes to self):
- Confirm final retirement date with legal/compliance (any contractual notice period?).
- Decide whether we auto-route after 01-15 by default or require opt-in; legal prefers opt-out only for non-enterprise.
- Need a short sign-off template for account execs to confirm migration plans (CS ops).
- Verify whether console will show per-account A/B sim results or just aggregate.

Slack + links to drop in the all-hands slides (placeholders):
- Slack: #product-announcements, #sre-ops, #cs-accounts, #inc-legacy-models.
- Doc links: CONFLUENCE-REDWOOD/MODEL-POLICY-2024, docs.redwood.ai/migration-guide-1.0->v2, github.com/redwood-inference/tooling/compat-router.

Risk notes (short):
- Regressions in output quality for small but vocal customers — prepare escalation path and temporary tuning knobs.
- Unexpected latency regressions for prefix-heavy workloads — KV cache behavior differs on new kernels.
- Sales churn risk if we mis-communicate timelines — require CS review of comms.

Last-minute prep for Friday (speaker checklist):
- 2 slides: Why / timeline / what we’re doing for customers.
- 1 backup slide: per-customer migration example (screenshots).
- 1 slide for Q&A hotspots + who to ping after (names + Slack channels).
- Rehearse with CEO + Product lead for 10 minutes on Thursday.

Notes to self: keep tone empathetic, emphasize support and optionality, avoid technical jargon for non-technical audience. Fall back to data when asked: we have benchmarking and per-account simulation — reference JIRA-ENG-4721.

Scratch ends. Use this to draft the final all-hands script (I'll convert to slides after sign-offs).
